### First BanCorp. Announces Earnings for the Quarter Ended September 30, 2026


October 22, 2026


- [Download (opens in new window)](https://s29.q4cdn.com/196528818/files/content_files/FBP-3Q26-Financial-Results-Press-Release.pdf)


SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico--(BUSINESS WIRE)--


First BanCorp. (the “Corporation” or “First BanCorp.”) (NYSE: FBP), the bank holding company for FirstBank Puerto Rico (“FirstBank” or “the Bank”), today reported a net income of $96.1 million, or $0.63 per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $96.1 million, or $0.62 per diluted share, for the second quarter of 2026, and $100.5 million, or $0.63 per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2025.


***Aurelio Alemán, President and Chief Executive Officer of First BanCorp, commented:*** *“We delivered another quarter of strong core performance, highlighted by a return on average assets of 1.98%, a return on average equity of 19.5%, stable credit metrics, and healthy balance sheet trends against the backdrop of an increasingly volatile rate environment. These results demonstrate consistent execution against our strategic priorities, the resilience of our business model, and our commitment to soundness, profitability, and responsible growth.*


*Total loans grew 3.3% annualized on a linked-quarter basis, with growth across all our operating markets, particularly in the commercial segment, despite higher than prior quarter commercial repayments. Core deposits, excluding brokered and government deposits, increased by $120 million, while non-performing assets remained relatively flat compared with the prior quarter.*


*We continued advancing our multichannel strategy by combining our expanded Puerto Rico branch network with digital tools that provide clients a faster, more convenient, and seamless service experience. This commitment to innovation and client-centric digital solutions was recognized this quarter by Global Finance, which named us the “Best Digital User Experience in Latin America and Puerto Rico” and the “Best Digital Banking App in Puerto Rico.” We are very proud of this recognition, which reflects our associates' hard work and dedication to delivering the best digital banking experience for our clients.*


*Finally, we remain focused on allocating capital where it can generate the highest long-term returns for shareholders. We were also pleased to announce that our Board of Directors approved a new $350 million stock repurchase program and a 25% increase in our common stock dividend. We remain committed to thoughtful excess capital deployment while preserving flexibility to support organic growth and other franchise-enhancing opportunities.”*

**Results for the Third Quarter of 2026 compared to the Second Quarter of 2026**


**Profitability**


**Net income –** $96.1 million, or $0.63 per diluted share compared to $96.1 million, or $0.62 per diluted share.


**Income before income taxes** **–** $115.3 million compared to $120.2 million.


**Pre-tax, pre-provision income (Non-GAAP)** (1) **–** $129.9 million compared to $137.5 million.


**Net interest income –** $227.5 million compared to $229.1 million. The decrease was mostly related to $3.4 million in interest income recognized during the second quarter of 2026 from purchase discount and deferred fees accelerations, which accounted for approximately 7 basis points of the decrease in net interest margin, and an increase of $4.8 million in deposit costs. These variances were partially offset by higher commercial and construction loan balances, reinvestment of maturing debt securities in higher-yielding assets, and $1.3 million related to an additional day in the quarter. Net interest margin decreased to 4.73% compared to 4.87% driven by the aforementioned $3.4 million in interest income recognized in the second quarter of 2026 and an increase of 8 basis points in the cost of funds.


**Provision for credit losses –** $14.6 million compared to $17.3 million. The decrease in provision expense was mainly due to a reduction of $3.2 million in the provision for residential mortgage loans, mostly driven by updated historical loss experience resulting in a downward revision of estimated loss severities.


**Non-interest income –** $32.6 million compared to $35.7 million. The decrease mainly reflected $1.9 million in lower realized gains on purchased income tax credits and a $0.6 million gain from the sale of a fixed asset in the Florida region in the previous quarter.


**Non-interest expenses** – $130.2 million compared to $127.3 million, including an additional $2.8 million contingency reserve involving a commercial other real estate owned (“OREO”) property.


**Income tax expense** – $19.2 million compared to $24.1 million, mainly due to a lower estimated annual effective tax rate.


**Balance**


**Sheet**


**Total loans –** increased by $108.3 million to $13.4 billion, driven by commercial and industrial (“C&I”) loan growth. Total loan originations of $1.5 billion, down $238.5 million, mainly in commercial and construction loans, driven by $270.6 million in certain refinancings during the second quarter of 2026.


**Core deposits (other than brokered and government deposits) –** increased by $120.4 million to $13.4 billion, mainly in the Puerto Rico region, driven by a $253.0 million increase in time deposits, partially offset by a $132.6 million decrease in non-maturity deposits.


**Government deposits (fully collateralized) –** decreased by $76.7 million to $3.0 billion, of which $57.2 million was in the Puerto Rico region and $34.6 million was in the Virgin Islands region.


**Asset**


**Quality**


**Allowance for credit losses (“ACL”) coverage ratio –** amounted to 1.81% compared to 1.85%.


**Annualized net charge-offs to average loans ratio** **–** increased to 0.55% compared to 0.49%, primarily reflecting a $2.0 million increase in consumer loans and finance leases net charge-offs, mainly in the auto loan portfolio.


**Non-performing assets –** increased by $0.2 million to $114.1 million, driven by a $1.6 million increase in nonaccrual loans, primarily in auto loans, partially offset by a $1.3 million decrease in the OREO portfolio balance.


**Loans in early delinquency (30-89 days past due) –** increased by $12.1 million to $155.5 million, which included an $8.3 million matured construction loan that was fully repaid after September 30, 2026 and a $6.8 million increase in consumer loans and finance leases, mainly auto loans.

**Capital**


**Liquidity –** Cash and cash equivalents amounted to $462.7 million compared to $561.3 million. When adding $2.1 billion of free high-quality liquid securities that could be liquidated or pledged within one day and $1.1 billion in available lending capacity at the Federal Home Loan Bank (“FHLB”), available liquidity amounted to 19.15% of total assets compared to 19.60%.


**Capital –** Repurchased $50.0 million in common stock and declared $30.4 million in common stock dividends. Capital ratios exceeded required regulatory levels. The Corporation’s estimated total capital, common equity tier 1 (“CET1”) capital, tier 1 capital, and leverage ratios were 18.16%, 16.91%, 16.91%, and 11.71%, respectively, as of September 30, 2026. On a non-GAAP basis, the tangible common equity ratio(1) decreased to 9.55% compared to 10.08%, mainly due to a decrease in the fair value of available-for-sale debt securities.

Net interest income amounted to $227.5 million for the third quarter of 2026, a decrease of $1.6 million, compared to $229.1 million for the second quarter of 2026. The third quarter of 2026 included an increase of approximately $1.3 million associated with the effect of an additional day in the quarter. The decrease in net interest income reflects the following:


- A $4.8 million increase in interest expense on interest-bearing deposits, primarily reflecting higher average balances of non-brokered time deposits and brokered certificates of deposit (“CDs”), which increased $195.1 million and $98.1 million, respectively, as well as higher rates paid on interest-bearing checking and saving accounts, mainly government deposits. The average cost of interest-bearing checking and saving accounts increased 7 basis points to 1.33%, while the cost excluding government deposits increased 3 basis points to 0.69%.


Partially offset by:


- A $3.0 million net increase in interest income on loans, driven by a $2.6 million increase in interest income on commercial and construction loans, reflecting $3.1 million associated with a $178.9 million increase in the average balance and $1.1 million from an additional day in the third quarter of 2026, partially offset by $1.6 million resulting from the acceleration of net deferred fees associated with the refinancing of a C&I loan in the Puerto Rico region during the second quarter of 2026.


- A $0.1 million net increase in interest income on investment securities and interest-earning cash balances, reflecting higher yields from reinvesting maturities of debt securities in higher-yielding debt securities, partially offset by $1.8 million resulting from the acceleration of the unamortized purchase discount on a municipal bond refinanced during the second quarter of 2026 into a shorter-term commercial loan structure.


Net interest margin for the third quarter of 2026 was 4.73% compared to 4.87% for the previous quarter. The decrease mainly reflected a shift in the mix of interest-bearing deposits toward higher-yielding options, such as time deposits, and a 7 basis points reduction from prior quarter purchase discount and deferred fee accelerations while higher rates paid on interest-bearing government non-maturity deposits were offset by higher yields from the reinvestment of maturing debt securities.

Non-interest expenses amounted to $130.2 million in the third quarter of 2026, an increase of $2.9 million, from $127.3 million in the second quarter of 2026. Non-interest expenses for the third quarter of 2026 reflect the following significant variances:


- A $2.6 million increase in other non-interest expenses, primarily reflecting an additional $2.8 million contingency reserve in connection with an adverse court ruling involving a commercial OREO property in the U.S. Virgin Islands, recorded as part of other non-interest expenses.


- A $0.9 million increase in credit and debit card processing expenses, mainly due to credit and debit card expense reimbursements recognized during the second quarter of 2026.


- A $0.8 million increase in employees’ compensation and benefits expenses, mainly associated with the effect of annual salary merit increases and an additional working day in the third quarter of 2026.


Partially offset by:


- A $1.7 million decrease in professional service fees, mostly driven by lower legal fees recorded as part of other professional fees, as well as lower collections, appraisals and other credit-related expenses and outsourcing fees, partially offset by higher consulting fees.


**INCOME TAXES**


The Corporation recorded an income tax expense of $19.2 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $24.1 million for the second quarter of 2026. The decrease in income tax expense was driven by a lower estimated annual effective tax rate mostly related to higher than previously forecasted business activities with preferential tax treatment under the Puerto Rico tax code.


For the year, the Corporation’s annual effective tax rate was estimated at 20.5% for the third quarter of 2026, compared to 21.5% for the second quarter of 2026. As of September 30, 2026, the Corporation had a net deferred tax asset of $135.0 million, net of a valuation allowance of $88.3 million, compared to a net deferred tax asset of $142.0 million, net of a valuation allowance of $75.6 million as of June 30, 2026.

Variances in credit quality metrics:


- Total non-performing assets increased by $0.2 million to $114.1 million as of September 30, 2026, driven by a $1.6 million increase in nonaccrual loans, primarily in auto loans, partially offset by a $1.3 million decrease in the OREO portfolio balance, mainly attributable to the sale of a $0.9 million residential property in the Florida region. In addition, the increase in nonaccrual loans included the migration of a $1.8 million commercial mortgage loan in the Florida region to nonaccrual status during the third quarter of 2026, partially offset by $1.3 million in repayments on a nonaccrual C&I loan in the Puerto Rico region in the food retail industry.


- Inflows to nonaccrual loans held for investment were $34.5 million in the third quarter of 2026, down $6.2 million from $40.7 million in the second quarter of 2026. Inflows to nonaccrual commercial and construction loans decreased $12.8 million to $2.3 million, reflecting the impact of a $14.8 million C&I relationship in the Florida region that migrated to nonaccrual status in the second quarter of 2026, partially offset by the aforementioned $1.8 million commercial mortgage loan inflow in the third quarter. Inflows to nonaccrual consumer loans increased $5.6 million to $28.4 million, while nonaccrual residential mortgage loan inflows increased $1.0 million to $3.8 million. See *Early Delinquency* below ** for additional information.


- Adversely classified commercial and construction loans increased by $15.8 million to $103.0 million as of September 30, 2026, compared to $87.2 million as of June 30, 2026, driven by the downgrade of a $13.1 million participated C&I loan in the Florida region that is part of the Shared National Credit program.


**Early Delinquency**


Total loans held for investment in early delinquency (i.e., 30-89 days past due accruing loans, as defined in regulatory reporting instructions) amounted to $155.5 million as of September 30, 2026, an increase of $12.1 million, compared to $143.4 million as of June 30, 2026, driven by a $6.8 million increase in consumer loans and finance leases, primarily in the auto loan portfolio, and a $4.6 million increase in the commercial and construction loan portfolios. The increase in commercial and construction loans was primarily driven by the aforementioned $8.3 million matured construction loan for which the Corporation received full repayment after September 30, 2026, and a $1.2 million matured commercial mortgage relationship in the process of renewal for which the Corporation continues to receive payments from the borrower. These increases were partially offset by the renewal of two matured commercial mortgage loans totaling $3.1 million and the aforementioned $1.8 million commercial mortgage loan that migrated to nonaccrual status.

**Non-GAAP Financial Measures**


*Tangible Common Equity Ratio and Tangible Book Value per Common Share*


The tangible common equity ratio and tangible book value per common share are non-GAAP financial measures that management believes are generally used by the financial community to evaluate capital adequacy. Tangible common equity is total common equity less goodwill and other intangible assets. Tangible assets are total assets less goodwill and other intangible assets. Tangible common equity ratio is tangible common equity divided by tangible assets. Tangible book value per common share is tangible assets divided by common shares outstanding. Refer to *Statement of Financial Condition – Tangible Common Equity (Non-GAAP)* for a reconciliation of the Corporation’s total stockholders’ equity and total assets in accordance with GAAP to the non-GAAP financial measures of tangible common equity and tangible assets, respectively. Management uses and believes that many stock analysts use the tangible common equity ratio and tangible book value per common share in conjunction with other more traditional bank capital ratios to compare the capital adequacy of banking organizations with significant amounts of goodwill or other intangible assets, typically stemming from the use of the purchase method of accounting for mergers and acquisitions. Accordingly, the Corporation believes that disclosure of these financial measures may be useful to investors. Neither tangible common equity nor tangible assets, or the related measures, should be considered in isolation or as a substitute for stockholders’ equity, total assets, or any other measure calculated in accordance with GAAP. Moreover, the manner in which the Corporation calculates its tangible common equity, tangible assets, and any other related measures may differ from that of other companies reporting measures with similar names.


*Adjusted Net Income, Adjusted Non-Interest Expenses, Adjusted Income Tax Expense, and Adjusted Earnings Per Share*


To supplement the Corporation’s financial statements presented in accordance with GAAP, the Corporation uses, and believes that investors benefit from disclosure of, non-GAAP financial measures that reflect adjustments to net income, non-interest expenses, income tax expense, and adjusted earnings per share to exclude Special Items.


*Adjusted Pre-Tax, Pre-Provision Income*


Adjusted pre-tax, pre-provision income is a non-GAAP performance metric that management uses and believes that investors may find useful in analyzing underlying performance trends, particularly in times of economic stress, including as a result of natural catastrophes or health epidemics. Adjusted pre-tax, pre-provision income, as defined by management, represents income before income taxes adjusted to exclude the provisions for credit losses on loans, unfunded loan commitments and debt securities. In addition, from time to time, earnings are also adjusted for certain items that management believes are not reflective of core operating performance, which are regarded as Special Items.


*Net Interest Income, Interest Rate Spread, and Net Interest Margin on a Tax-Equivalent Basis*


Net interest income, interest rate spread, and net interest margin are reported on a tax-equivalent basis in order to provide to investors additional information about the Corporation’s net interest income that management uses and believes should facilitate comparability and analysis of the periods presented. The tax-equivalent adjustment to net interest income recognizes the income tax savings when comparing taxable and tax-exempt assets and assumes a marginal income tax rate. Income from tax-exempt earning assets is increased by an amount equivalent to the taxes that would have been paid if this income had been taxable at statutory rates. Refer to Tables 4 and 5 in the accompanying tables (Exhibit A) for a reconciliation of the Corporation’s net interest income on a tax-equivalent basis. Management believes that it is a standard practice in the banking industry to present net interest income, interest rate spread, and net interest margin on a fully tax-equivalent basis. This adjustment puts all earning assets, most notably tax-exempt securities and tax-exempt loans, on a common basis that management believes facilitates comparison of results to the results of peers.
